text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-tail p99 and p95 SLO breaches detected in prod-us-west-2 cluster (svc=runtime). Auto-triage tags: paging, kernel-alloc, decode-latency. Alert runbook: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/paging

maya: seeing big p99 spikes starting ~09:04 UTC, correlates with last kernel build rollout at 08:50. p99 decode went from ~220ms -> 2.1s on GPU nodes with TRT8.

james: confirmed. Metrics snapshot: `runtime.decode.p99 = 2100ms`, `streaming.tail.p95 = 1400ms`, error rate unchanged. Heatmap shows concentrated on machines with kernel v5.15.41-custom and new compileflags `-fast-kv`.

li: flagging that the TRT/FlashAttention rollout to the canary pool finished at 08:48, then the kernel pack distributed at 08:49. I have logs from node gpu-w-13 with repeated page-evict stalls.

maya: pasting the decode tail from gpubox logs:

```
2026-03-15T09:06:12Z runtime: decode: begin seq=1 ctx=kv
2026-03-15T09:06:12Z kernel: mmap failed PREFETCH: page_fault stall 312ms
2026-03-15T09:06:12Z runtime: decode: blocking for kv fetch 315ms
2026-03-15T09:06:13Z qkern: flash_attn_dispatch: fallback to safe path
2026-03-15T09:06:13Z runtime: decode: end seq=1 duration=2187ms
```

sophie: any known customers hitting errors or timeouts? CS reports a couple of elevated latency complaints from "AcmeHealth" and "Chatly" since ~09:10 UTC. We're prepping comms if this becomes outage.

mike: I'm on it. Suggest immediate mitigation steps: 1) move traffic off kernel-rollout nodes via routing policy, 2) revert compile flag `-fast-kv`, 3) if needed, rollback TRT8 package to previous. Can we do a quick routing bump?

james: agree. Eng-sre can shift 30% of streaming traffic to older pool (pool-legacy) to buy time. @deploy-bot can you run policy patch?

deploy-bot: Received request to update routing policy. Patch ID: rp-20260315-01. Preview: shift 30% streaming traffic from pool-canary -> pool-legacy. ETA: 60s.

ONCALL-HANDBOOK-BOT: Reminder: for paging-related p99s use mitigation checklist -> 1) route away, 2) collect kv/cache stats, 3) validate no config drift. Link: https://redwood/ops/paging-mitigation

li: while routing flips, I'm collecting per-process page-fault counters and kernel oops logs. Early grep shows many `shmmu` faults during `nvdec` sessions. Could be new kernel memory reclaim heuristics interacting with KV cache.

maya: rolling metrics after routing change (09:11): p99 down to 1.4s, p95 down to 900ms. Good sign but still above SLOs. We'll need the flag revert.

mike: to revert compile flag we need a rebuild of the kernel package without `-fast-kv`. I can trigger a hotpatch build and staged deploy to canary pool only. Command I will run: `./build-kernel --profile=stable --remove-flag=fast-kv --tag=hotfix-20260315`

james: please collect perf traces before the hotpatch goes live so we can compare. Use `perf record` vs `trace-cmd` for a 30s window on impacted hosts. Store to /var/tmp/paging-traces/4467890123/

mike: starting build now. ETA ~7m. Noted.

sophie: alerting AcmeHealth CSM that we're investigating and have mitigations in flight. Keeping message informal: "We are aware of increased response times in US-West, routing adjustments made and a patch being prepared. We'll follow up in 30 minutes."

li: pulled a perf snapshot from gpu-w-13 before routing; attaching diff snippet:

```
# perf top diff (hot functions)
- flash_attn_kernel_dispatch +42%
- gpu_kv_cache_lookup +35%
+ page_fault_handler +58%
+ mm_reclaim_enter +20%
```

maya: that strongly suggests the kernel path change caused more page faults under the new compile flags. If hotfix rebuilds without `-fast-kv` shows lower `page_fault_handler` time, we can promote.

deploy-bot: Build hotfix `hotfix-20260315` completed and pushed to staging repo. Initiating canary deploy to 3 nodes (gpucan-01..03).

mike: canary live on gpucan-01..03. Observability note: add `kernel.alloc.trace` at DEBUG for these nodes for next 20m. `kubectl annotate node gpucan-01 observability=kernel-debug`

james: monitoring canary metrics. After hotfix canary (09:28) p99 on canary nodes dropped to 260ms and page_fault_handler CPU down 80%. Non-canary nodes still high.

maya: propose staged rollout: 20% more every 5m while observing p99 and pagefault counts. Any objections?

li: no objections. I'll keep collecting tail logs. If we see a regression on other kernels, abort.

sophie: continuing customer comms. I'll prepare a short status update in 30m and advise CS to hold on escalation until we finish staged rollout.

mike: starting staged rollout now. Patch: remove `-fast-kv` (hotfix-20260315) -> pool-canary -> pool-prod in 4 waves.

incident-bot: Update: SLO breach cleared at 09:41 UTC for overall cluster after hotfix rollout. p99 back to baseline ~210ms. Incident severity: S2. Next steps: postmortem, root cause analysis, test matrix for kernel flags + KV cache interaction, and customer RCA draft.

james: I'll open the incident ticket and assign owners for RCA (runtime: mike/ li, infra: maya). Target postmortem in 72h.

sophie: I'll coordinate customer-facing RCA with legal and CS.

maya: adding note to rollouts: gate kernel-compose builds with KV-load synthetic tests that simulate streaming prefix caching. We'll add it to CI.

incident-bot: Incident closed to monitoring (automated) at 09:49 UTC.
